patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined in 2022. Two pregnancies under outside obstetric care: a term delivery in 2024 with presentation uncertain in labor, then eclampsia at 35 weeks in October 2025 with postpartum labetalol that the practice stopped in December 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to establish here. Moved her care from her old office, which she says was too far to get to after school lets out. 26 y/o F, teacher, Medicaid. No current health problems per caller, takes nothing daily. Offered first available new pt physical 9/13 at 3:45, accepted. Sent intake forms + records release through the portal. Reminded to bring insurance card.

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT, PREVENTIVE

26 yo woman here to set up primary care. Previously seen at a primary care office in another town; release signed today. Feels well. No concerns she wants to raise. Periods regular, no pelvic or breast symptoms. Not currently trying for pregnancy but she and her partner have talked about it for the next year or two.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations. Never pregnant.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: her mother had preeclampsia and had to be delivered at 36 weeks. A maternal aunt had eclamptic seizures with her first baby. Otherwise nothing she knows of.
Social: teaches second grade at a public elementary school. Lives with her partner. Never a smoker. Does not drink. No drug use. Walks most evenings.
Prevention: last Pap about two years ago at her old office, told it was fine. Thinks she had the HPV shots in middle school. Tdap as a young adult; records requested.

ROS: negative across systems.

Exam: well-appearing, pleasant. Vitals as recorded, BP normal. HEENT normal, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without swelling. Skin clear. Mood and affect normal. PHQ-2 is 0.

Assessment and plan:
1. Adult preventive care. Baseline CBC, CMP and lipids. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agreed. Pap not due until next year; will confirm the date from her old records.
2. Family history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (mother, aunt). Discussed that this matters if she becomes pregnant, and that she should tell her obstetrician early. Folate-containing prenatal vitamin once she starts trying.
3. Vaccines: flu and bivalent COVID booster given, tolerated.
RTC one year for physical.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jada, everything from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol all in good range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Nice to meet you this week.

documents.title: RE: Your Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you!! Good to know. My arm was a little sore from the shots yesterday but I'm fine now.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Busy start of the year with a new class but otherwise doing well. No complaints. Cycles regular, LMP about 2 weeks ago. She and her partner are hoping to conceive in the coming year.

No meds, NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Family hx unchanged (mother preeclampsia, delivered 36 wk; maternal aunt eclampsia).

Exam: NAD. BP normal today. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen benign. Breast exam normal, no masses or nodes. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix appears normal, Pap obtained. No adnexal tenderness. Legs no swelling.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap today (3-year interval, last 2020 normal). Labs last year normal, nothing needed today.
- Preconception: start a prenatal vitamin with folate when she begins trying, she'll buy one or message me for a script. Again reviewed family history of preeclampsia; she should mention it at her first OB visit.
- Flu and updated COVID given.
Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Pap Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap test was normal. With your history, the next one is due in three years. Have a good week!

documents.title: Positive Pregnancy Test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! I took a test this weekend and it was positive, then took another one to be sure. First day of my last period was Oct 27. I haven't started the prenatal vitamin yet, oops. What do I do next? Do I need to come in or go straight to an OB?

documents.title: RE: Positive Pregnancy Test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Jada! By your dates you're about 5 1/2 weeks along. You can go straight to obstetrics; I've put in the referral today and their office will call you to set up the first visit, usually around 8 weeks. I also sent a prenatal vitamin with DHA to your pharmacy, one a day starting now. Please let them know about your mom's and aunt's history at the first visit. Call us any time with questions or if you have bleeding or bad cramping.

documents.title: Referral Follow-up
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt to check that the OB referral went through. She had her first OB appointment last week, ultrasound matched her dates, due early August. Feeling queasy in the afternoons but eating and drinking ok. Taking the prenatal vitamin. Referral closed.

medications.sig: Chew 1 tablet twice daily as needed for heartburn

documents.title: Heartburn Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, quick one. I've had heartburn most nights the last couple weeks (24 weeks now!). My OB said I can take calcium carbonate chewables, 500 mg up to twice a day when I need it. Just wanted you to have it on my list. Otherwise all good, baby is kicking a lot.

documents.title: RE: Heartburn Question
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Jada, added to your medication list as an as-needed med. Dr. reviewed, no concerns. Smaller dinners and not lying down right after eating can help too.

documents.title: Baby News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: She's here! Our daughter was born Friday the 2nd, right on her due date. Contractions started early that morning and when they checked me they couldn't tell if she was head down or breech, which was scary for a bit. They did an ultrasound and she was head down, so I delivered normally that afternoon. We came home Sunday. Both of us doing well, nursing is going ok. Just wanted to let you know!

documents.title: RE: Baby News
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations to you both! So glad everyone is well. Keep up the prenatal vitamin while you're nursing. Once you've had your postpartum OB check, let's get you in for your physical in September.

documents.title: Obstetric Delivery Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, LABOR AND DELIVERY — DELIVERY SUMMARY (copy to primary care)
Admitted: 08/02/2024. Discharged: 08/04/2024.

28 y/o G1 at 40w0d by early ultrasound, seen for regular contractions about 5 min apart over 2 hours, moderately painful and getting stronger. Prenatal care with our office, no complications this pregnancy. Medications: prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; calcium carbonate 500 mg BID prn heartburn. NKDA.

On arrival BP 120/78, HR 88, T 37.2 C. Fundus appropriate for dates, FHR 140 heard low on the abdomen. Cervix 3/80; presenting part could not be clearly identified on exam, cephalic vs breech unclear. Bedside ultrasound: cephalic, vertex.

Course: labor progressed without augmentation. Spontaneous vaginal delivery, viable female infant, uncomplicated. Postpartum course routine; BPs normal throughout stay.

Discharge diagnoses: term pregnancy, delivered; fetal presentation uncertain in labor, cephalic on ultrasound.
Discharge meds: continue prenatal vitamin.
Follow-up: postpartum visit with obstetrics in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 7 weeks postpartum. Baby (daughter, 8/2) with her today in a car seat, thriving. Had her OB postpartum check last week, told all healed. Plans to return to teaching in November.

Delivery: term, presentation unclear on exam in labor, ultrasound showed vertex, then an uncomplicated vaginal birth. Summary from the hospital is in the chart. BP normal through the pregnancy and after per pt.

Sleeping in pieces as expected. Mood good, partner very involved. Breastfeeding, going well. Bleeding has stopped.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; calcium carbonate chews, hasn't needed them since delivery but wants to keep them on hand.
NKDA. No tobacco, no alcohol.
Tdap given at OB in June, added to record.

Exam: well, tired-appearing but bright. BP normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Thyroid normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. No leg swelling.
PHQ-9: 2.

A/P
- Postpartum, doing well. CBC today. Pregnancy and the labor presentation issue resolved on the problem list.
- Continue prenatal vitamin while nursing.
- Mood screen reassuring; told her to reach out if that changes over the next months.
- Pap not due until 2026.
- Flu and updated COVID today (both fine while breastfeeding).
Physical next fall.

documents.title: Pregnant Again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Surprise! Positive test tonight. Last period started Feb 14. A little sooner than we planned but we're happy. Still taking the prenatal vitamin every day. Can you send me back to the same OB office?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant Again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! That puts you at about 6 weeks. Referral to the same obstetrics office is in, and I flagged your family history for them again. Keep the vitamin going. Let us know if you need anything before you're seen.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: OB office confirmed pt was seen 4/7 for her new OB visit. Referral marked complete.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called to let us know she was in the hospital. Sunday evening at home she had a seizure, partner saw it and drove her straight to the ED. Had been getting headaches and some blurry vision for a few days before and hadn't called anyone. ED told her it was eclampsia. Got magnesium and IV BP meds, then moved to L&D, induced, and delivered a baby boy Monday at 35 weeks. Both home now and doing ok. Discharged yesterday on labetalol 200 mg twice a day; OB wants a BP check within a week. No headache, vision fine, no seizure since. Has a home cuff from OB.
Booked with PCP Wed 10/29 at 9:20. Asked her to call 911 for any seizure, severe headache, vision change or chest pain/SOB. Requested ED and hospital records.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 29F, 10 days after an eclamptic seizure at 35w2d (LMP 2/14). Brought to a regional ED 10/19 after a generalized seizure at home lasting about a minute, then postictal. Several days of headaches and intermittent blurred vision beforehand. Per pt she was treated with magnesium and IV labetalol, admitted to L&D, induced, and had a vaginal delivery of a boy 10/20. Infant home and feeding. She went home 10/23 on labetalol 200 mg BID. No discharge summary yet; ED/hospital records requested 10/24.

Since home: no headaches, no visual symptoms, no RUQ pain, no SOB. Ankles were puffy last week and are better. Home BPs mostly 130s/80s. Taking labetalol twice daily, some lightheadedness getting up at night, no falls. Pumping and nursing.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID (hospital), prenatal vitamin with DHA daily, calcium carbonate prn (not using).
NKDA. Tdap (late Aug) and flu (end of Sept) given at OB, added to record.
FHx: mother preeclampsia, maternal aunt eclampsia.

O: BP 136/86 on recheck. Alert, oriented, conversant, no deficits. Fundi not examined. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, fundus below the umbilicus, nontender. Trace ankle edema both sides. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric, no clonus.

A/P
1. Eclampsia, postpartum. Neurologically back to baseline. BP acceptable on labetalol. CBC and CMP today to check counts, kidney and liver numbers after the admission. Keep labetalol 200 BID. Home BP twice daily, send readings in 2-3 weeks. Return precautions for headache, vision change, seizure, BP 160/110 or higher: 911/ED.
2. Pregnancy delivered; removed from list.
3. Recurrence and long-term risk: she'll need early obstetric care in any future pregnancy, and yearly BP and cardiovascular checks after this. Will talk more once she's recovered.
Follow-up in about 8 weeks, sooner by BP readings.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jada, yesterday's labs are all normal: blood count, platelets, kidney function and liver tests. Keep the labetalol as is and send me your home readings in a couple of weeks.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPT — PHYSICIAN NOTE (faxed copy)
DOS 10/19/2025

CC: seizure at home.
HPI: 29 y/o G2P1 at 35w2d, brought in by her partner, who saw her go rigid and then shake for roughly one minute while sitting on the couch, followed by confusion and sleepiness. He says she has complained of headaches and some blurred vision over the last several days; did not seek care. No recent illness, fever or injury. Prior pregnancy: term vaginal delivery 8/2024, presentation unclear in labor; prenatal course that pregnancy was normal.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; calcium carbonate 500 mg BID prn heartburn. Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother preeclampsia, delivered at 36 wk; maternal aunt eclampsia in first pregnancy.
SH: teacher, never smoker, no alcohol.

VS: T 36.7, HR 96, RR 18, BP 162/106.
Exam: postictal, rouses to voice. 2+ pitting edema bilateral lower extremities. Fetal monitoring: reactive NST.
UA: protein 3+. Remaining labs pending at time of note.

Impression: eclampsia, 35 weeks.
ED course: magnesium sulfate loading dose and infusion; IV labetalol for BP. OB at bedside. No further seizure activity in the department.
Disposition: admitted to Labor & Delivery.

documents.title: Home BP Readings
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Here are my numbers for the last 2 weeks. Mornings mostly 118-126 over 72-80, evenings about the same, highest was 128/82. Taking the labetalol twice a day. No headaches. The dizziness at night is gone. Baby is gaining weight!

documents.title: RE: Home BP Readings
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: These look great. Stay on the labetalol for now and keep checking once a day. At your visit next month we'll likely be able to come off it. Glad the little one is growing.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Blood Pressure Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, ~10 weeks after eclampsia and delivery at 35 wk.

Feels like herself. No headaches, vision changes, swelling or chest symptoms. Home readings over the last month mostly 110s/70s on labetalol 200 BID, a few in the low 100s systolic with some morning lightheadedness. OB postpartum visit done earlier this month, told she's healed. Still nursing. Sleeping when the baby sleeps. Mood ok, PHQ-9 3. ED note received 11/6 and reviewed; no discharge summary has come.

Meds: labetalol 200 BID, prenatal vitamin with DHA daily, calcium carbonate prn (hasn't used).

Exam: BP 116/74, HR regular. Well-appearing. Heart and lungs normal. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. Blood pressure after eclampsia, now normal. Stop labetalol today (low dose, readings low-normal). Check home BP daily for 2 weeks and message me; restart if consistently 140/90 or more. Eclampsia closed on the problem list, history of preeclampsia added.
2. Long-term risk: a hypertensive pregnancy roughly doubles later heart and blood pressure risk. Plan BP at least yearly here, lipids today, and a yearly physical. Any future pregnancy: let OB know early so they can plan prevention from the start.
3. Prenatal vitamin continues while nursing.
Physical next fall.

documents.title: Cholesterol Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your cholesterol panel from Friday is in a healthy range. We'll repeat it every few years. Don't forget to send home BPs in two weeks.

documents.title: BPs Off Labetalol
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two weeks off the labetalol. Readings have been 112-124 over 70-78, nothing over 125. Feeling good and no more dizzy mornings.

documents.title: RE: BPs Off Labetalol
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Perfect, those are normal. You can stop checking daily; a few readings a month is plenty. See you in the fall for your physical.

documents.title: Refill: Prenatal Vitamin
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy e-request, prenatal vitamin with DHA daily. Pt still breastfeeding per 12/26 note. Refilled x1 year.
